properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 22 at 2:00AM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
Elevated fire weather conditions can be expected across portions
of southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi this afternoon and
Friday afternoon. Relative humidity values are forecast to drop
into the 25 to 35 percent range. The 20 ft wind forecast is at or
less than 10 mph, which will limit critical fire weather
conditions or at least the effective spread of fires that may
ignite.

Numerous local burn bans remain in place across LA and MS due to
ongoing drought conditions. This includes East Feliciana, St.
Helena, Tangipahoa, and Washington Parishes along with Wilkinson,
Amite, Pike, and now Walthall Counties. Regardless, outdoor
burning is strongly not recommended this afternoon, and all local
restrictions followed.

Additional statements, Fire Weather Watches or Red Flag Warnings
will be possible in the upcoming days as drought conditions
worsen, relative humidity values remain low during the afternoon,
and eventually winds begin to increase, especially this weekend.

NWSheadline: ELEVATED FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS TODAY AND INTO THE WEEKEND

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 21 at 11:49PM PDT until October 22 at 1:45AM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...South Central Inyo County in south central California...

* WHEN...Until 145 AM PDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1149 PM PDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain due to thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly in the advisory area. Up to 0.5 inches
of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Panamint Springs and Homewood Canyon-Valley Wells.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 21 at 11:39PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
At 1137 PM PDT, Doppler radar was tracking strong thunderstorms along
a line extending from 7 miles southeast of Cuyama to Rose Valley to
Camarillo. Movement was northeast at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts of 50 to 55 mph. Small chance for a brief, weak
tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Oxnard...
Eastern Ventura...
Camarillo...
Ojai...
Santa Paula...
Rose Valley...
Lockwood Valley...
Meiners Oaks...
Reyes Peak...
Old Man Mountain...
Ventucopa...
Highway 33 between Wheeler Springs and Rose Valley Road...
Alamo Mountain...
Topatopa Peak...
Frazier Mountain...
Highway 33 from Lockwood Valley Road to the Santa Barbara County
line...
El Rio...
Lake Casitas...
and Interstate 5 over the Grapevine.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with these storms and may lead
to localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

cloud to ground lightning is occurring with these storms.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.

properties.areaDesc: Inland Sussex; Delaware Beaches; Ocean; Coastal Ocean
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 22 at 2:34AM EDT until October 22 at 10:00AM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...In Delaware, Inland Sussex and Delaware Beaches. In
New Jersey, Ocean and Coastal Ocean.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM EDT this morning.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most
vulnerable roads in coastal and bayside communities, and along
inland tidal waterways. Some partial or full road closures are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Greatest impacts will be in the back bays.
Lingering spotty minor tidal flooding is possible with this
evening's high tide cycles.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.
